findings.scope: Exactly the class C_2 of the claim: finite bipartite graphs with at least one edge, no cycle of length four, and some bipartition (X,Y) with every X-vertex of degree at most two. The equivalence is with Problem 1.5 for all finite simple base graphs with an edge (base graphs may be disconnected or have isolated vertices; the construction produces base graphs without isolated vertices, which does not restrict the problem since isolated base vertices become isolated pattern vertices, harmless by the isolated-vertex remark). The girth-six graphs outside C_2 (every bipartition has a vertex of degree at least three on each side), the bridge between the two parts of the case split, and the root decision are untouched, as the proof file states in Section 5. Section 5 item 2 (transfer of known cases, including Zhao 2026 Proposition 1.4) is a remark relying on sources not delivered here and is not part of the approved equivalence.
findings.statement: The subject is a checkpoint of kind `reduction` (milestone `c2-reduces-to-problem-1-5`). What is established, and what this approval covers, is Proposition B of the proof artifact (digest ac6948f3...): the claim on C_2 (for every finite bipartite H with an edge, no 4-cycle, and a bipartition in which one side has all degrees at most two, and every graphon W, t(H,W) >= t(K_2,W)^{e(H)}) holds if and only if the 1-subdivision S(F) of every finite simple graph F with at least one edge is Sidorenko (Problem 1.5 of Conlon, Kim, Lee and Lee, as stated verbatim in the delivered full text, digest a662797f...). The inequality on C_2 itself is NOT proved by this result, and the checkpoint does not assert it; obligations 000001-000004 remain open. I independently checked every step: (1) graphon form and finite-host form are equivalent for each H (step graphons one way; cut-distance approximation and the counting lemma the other way); (2) the tensor power trick (hom counts multiply over tensor products of simple graphs; c^{1/k} -> 1); (3) the bounded-degree reduction (vertex splitting with t_v = ceil(deg(v)/Delta) copies, injectivity of pi∘h because each G-edge lifts to exactly one G'-edge and H has no isolated vertex, |V(G')| <= 2|V(G)|, |E(G')| = |E(G)|, max degree of G' <= Delta <= 4|E(G')|/|V(G')|, and the exponent h-2m <= 0 giving the factor 2^{h-2m}); the trick is applied afterwards over all hosts, so the order of the two reductions is sound; (4) Lemma A (<=): Hom(H,G) = sum over Hom(H-v,G) of deg(phi(u)); the Conlon-Kim-Lee-Lee Lemma 3.4 subgraph G_0 with n_0 >= 2^{-6}n and min degree >= d/4 has p(G_0) >= p/4, and the chain |Hom(H,G)| >= (d/4)|Hom(H-v,G_0)| >= (pn/4)(2^{-6}n)^{h-1}(p/4)^{m-1} = 4^{-m}2^{-6(h-1)}n^h p^m is arithmetically correct; Lemma A (=>) via |Hom(H,G)| <= 2d|Hom(H-v,G)| is also correct though unused; edgeless-host cases are handled; (5) Proposition B (i)=>(ii): S(F) has the subdivision vertices as a side of degree exactly two, and a 4-cycle x a x' b would force a double edge of F; (ii)=>(i): peeling X-vertices of degree <= 1 (degrees of X-vertices are stable because X is independent), then isolated Y-vertices, then rebuilding by Lemma A (<=) and the isolated-vertex remark; the residual H'' is empty (then H is a forest of stars, Sidorenko by Lemma A from the empty graph) or isomorphic to S(F) for the simple graph F on Y'' whose edges are the neighbourhoods of X''-vertices, simplicity of F being exactly the absence of 4-cycles. No gap found.
